subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a first-class Gateway control-plane and per-agent runtime split in core, and what narrow Phase 0/1 milestone should be approved first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the solution changes core architecture, public config/protocol shape, session ownership, runtime isolation, and security boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product contract or trust model safely.

options.title: Approve Narrow Phase 0/1 Design
options.body: Keep embedded mode as the default and first specify per-agent lifecycle, local process/runtime protocol, session-state ownership, and fail-closed security boundaries before container or Kubernetes execution.

options.title: Defer To Backend Slices
options.body: Keep this RFC as context while maintainers first review the worker-runtime isolation and execution-backend/profile PRs as narrower building blocks.

options.title: Pause Distributed Runtime Work
options.body: Do not sponsor core distributed runtime work until current Gateway stability, setup, and security priorities have more room.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Phase 0/1 Design
recommendation.body: Keep embedded mode as the default and first specify per-agent lifecycle, local process/runtime protocol, session-state ownership, and fail-closed security boundaries before container or Kubernetes execution.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across the affected Gateway/runtime seams and authored the open worker-runtime isolation experiment.
